title: What is the inverse of each number?
description: Two presses that bring the lift back to the start are called inverses, and a number and its inverse add up to zero. The inverse of each of the six given numbers is found by asking which press brings the lift back. Keeko thinks zero has no inverse because there is nothing to cancel, and zero added to zero breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: the inverse of a number is the number that adds to it to give zero. Watch for students who think zero has no inverse.

source: Write the inverses of these numbers: +4, −4, −3, 0, +2, −1.
video_script.why: A child learns to write the inverse of a number, because the inverse is the base of subtraction and of cancelling in every later sum.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lift, using the press that brings the lift back to the start for each given number
video_script.anchor: the lift of Ruhee, with each given number as a press from the ground floor
video_script.wrong_move: thinks zero cannot be cancelled because there is nothing there to cancel
video_script.payoff_line: To find an inverse, change the sign, and zero stays zero.

final_answer.spoken: the inverses are minus four, plus four, plus three, zero, minus two and plus one

names.Ruhee: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

maths_rules: A number and its inverse add up to 0.
video_script.design: One idea: the inverse is the press that brings the lift back to zero. One lift picture throughout; each pair is drawn as two arrows that end where they began. Keeko's doubt is broken by adding zero to zero.

beats.on_screen: title card Back to the Ground Floor; the lift of the tall block appears, and six press tags appear in a row: plus four, minus four, minus three, zero, plus two, minus one

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the lift appears
marks.six: the six press tags appear one by one
marks.ask: the question is written into the anchor band

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the lift in Ruhee.
<bookmark mark='six'/>It gives six numbers, plus four, minus four, minus three, zero, plus two and minus one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>For each number, which press brings the lift back to zero?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board while the child thinks

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the lift on the ground floor; an up arrow of three floors and a down arrow of three floors end where they began, and the two arrows are labelled inverse

marks.cancel: the lift rises three floors and drops three floors back to the ground floor
marks.name: the word inverse is written between the two arrows
marks.zero: the sum 0 is written beside the arrows

narration: <bookmark mark='cancel'/>Pressing plus three, and then minus three, brings the lift back to where it began.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Each of these two presses is called the inverse of the other.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Adding a number and its inverse always gives zero.

marks.given: the line Given is written on the working board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six numbers, plus four, minus four, minus three, zero, plus two and minus one.

beats.on_screen: To find: the inverse of each number

marks.find: the line To find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the inverse of each number.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: for +4 and +2, the lift must come down: +4 → −4; +2 → −2

marks.four: an up arrow of four floors gets a down arrow of four floors beside it
marks.two: an up arrow of two floors gets a down arrow of two floors beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step one, plus four needs minus four to get back to zero.
<bookmark mark='two'/>In the same way, plus two needs minus two.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: for −4, −3 and −1, the lift must go up: −4 → +4; −3 → +3; −1 → +1

marks.four: a down arrow of four floors gets an up arrow of four floors beside it
marks.three: a down arrow of three floors gets an up arrow of three floors beside it
marks.one: a down arrow of one floor gets an up arrow of one floor beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step two, minus four needs plus four.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Minus three needs plus three.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Minus one needs plus one.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: for 0, the lift does not move: 0 → 0

marks.zero: the lift stays still on the ground floor and 0 is written twice

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step three, zero needs no press to stay at zero, so zero is its own inverse.

marks.check: each pair is added and every sum shows 0

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check by adding each pair.
Every pair makes zero.

marks.ans: the answer line is boxed on the working board
marks.ans2: the pairs for minus three and zero are underlined
marks.ans3: the pairs for plus two and minus one are underlined
marks.pay: the signs are circled and the zero is left plain

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The inverse of plus four is minus four, and the inverse of minus four is plus four.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>The inverse of minus three is plus three, and the inverse of zero is zero.
<bookmark mark='ans3'/>The inverse of plus two is minus two, and the inverse of minus one is plus one.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>To find an inverse, change the sign, and zero stays zero.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the lift
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says zero has no inverse; 0 + 0 = 0 is written under the bubble and the bubble is struck through
beats.colours: warning colour for the struck bubble
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks zero has no inverse, because there is nothing to cancel.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>But zero added to zero is still zero, so zero cancels itself.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Every number has an inverse, and the inverse of zero is zero.
